questions.question: In story S4 (Handlers: new signature, chat/reaction/delete-edit re-pointing and sender binding), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/chatHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/reactionHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/deleteEditHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/groupRumorDispatch.ts (new); app/src/lib/marmot/chatPersistence.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/handlers/*.test.ts and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `handlers` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S4 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S4's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/chatHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/reactionHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/deleteEditHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/groupRumorDispatch.ts (new); app/src/lib/marmot/chatPersistence.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/handlers/*.test.ts)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S4 implementation match the intent of its scope (Define the handler input {groupId,eventId,rumor,sender}, implement GroupHistoryHandlers dispatch/retract for the chat, reaction and delete/edit handlers (re-pointed beside the old registerHandlers path), idempotent by event id, message-store bumps driven from handler completion, own-echo confirmatio) and respect its exclusions (Poll/profile/profile-request/announcement handlers (S5); Retract unit assertions for polls/reactions/votes (S5))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S4 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

AC-HIST-10: Message-type store bumps (chat, reaction, poll, delete/edit) MUST be driven from handler completion inside `append`/`withdraw`; `group.onNotification` MUST drive only member, admin, name and disband resync. A test emitting a `message` notification only MUST leave message stores unchanged; a test emitting `members` MUST NOT bump message stores. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-FORGE-1: Library harness with two real clients (Alice, Mallory) in one group: a rumor whose inner `pubkey` is Alice's but sent by Mallory's MLS leaf MUST never reach the sink's handlers and MUST never be rendered (chat store has no row for it). A genuine Alice message MUST be rendered attributed to Alice. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-FORGE-2: e2e: a group chat message sent through the app by Bob renders in Alice's UI attributed to Bob. The pre-existing impersonation exposure noted in `security_group_message_impersonation` MUST be closed (covered by AC-FORGE-1). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [e2e:groups-identity (kept), harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-WDR-6: Effects already emitted (bell, known-peers additions, follow-up sends) MUST NOT be undone by `withdraw`: a test that appended then withdrew a message from a new peer MUST still find the peer in known-peers, and MUST NOT show a user-facing notice (no toast call). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

chatHandler.ts createChatGroupHandler.dispatch decides 'own message' by comparing the sink `sender` with env.selfPubkeyHex. Show that a peer-sent rumor whose inner pubkey is the local account's is NOT treated as an own echo (bell still rings, onOwnEcho not called) and that no file under handlers/ reads the rumor's pubkey (groupRumorDispatch.test.ts 'own-message guard is keyed on the sender'; handlersRumorPubkeyBoundary.test.ts).

createChatGroupHandler/createReactionGroupHandler/createDeleteEditGroupHandler take REQUIRED retract/own-lifecycle ports (removeMessages, recomputeUnread, rememberKnownPeer, onOwnEcho, onOwnWithdrawn, retractDeleteEditSignal, retractReaction). Confirm that S5/S6/S18 supply real implementations (retractReaction, retractDeleteEditSignal, onOwnWithdrawn/onOwnEcho, recomputeUnread over initUnreadCounts) and that no composition root wires them as no-ops, since S4 only fixture-tests them.

AC-WDR-6 asserts 'no user-facing notice'. The handler deps expose no toast/notice channel; the test pins the exact dep call sequence of a withdraw (removeMessages, recomputeUnread, setChatVersion). Confirm the composition root (S18) does not add a notice to retract paths, and that createChatGroupHandler.dispatch's rememberKnownPeer (a behaviour addition required by AC-WDR-6's 'known-peers additions') is acceptable product-wise.
